_comment: GEPER example patient metadata file for --patient-meta / report/summary.py::generate_pdf(patient_meta=...). This entire file is OPTIONAL: if --patient-meta is omitted, or this file is missing/corrupt/malformed, the clinical PDF report safely falls back to a de-identified header showing only Sample ID and Run ID -- it never crashes the pipeline. India DPDP Act 2023 note (not HIPAA/GDPR -- GEPER is an India-market product): patient_name/dob/gender/physician are personal data once a real (non-de-identified) file like this is used. This file itself implements no consent/retention/access-control logic -- those must be handled by whatever system collects and stores this data upstream of GEPER. Real DPDP Act compliance sign-off must come from someone qualified to review the full data flow before production/hospital use.
_consent_comment: The 'consent' object below is OPTIONAL and independent of the fields above -- it is captured and surfaced verbatim (as 'patient_consent' in geper_results.json, and as extra rows in the clinical PDF/summary PDF headers when present) purely as METADATA. This is NOT a DPDP Act 2023 compliance guarantee: GEPER does not itself obtain, store, timestamp-verify, or manage withdrawal/erasure of consent -- it only records whatever this file states. The actual consent process (how/when/from whom consent was obtained), its durable storage, its retention period, and honoring any withdrawal request are entirely the deploying lab's responsibility, upstream of and outside GEPER. Omit 'consent' entirely (as in most real runs, e.g. a de-identified research sample) to leave 'patient_consent' explicitly null in the JSON output -- GEPER never fabricates a true/false consent value that wasn't actually stated.
